title: Count Pairs in Two Arrays
statement: You are given two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2` of the same length `n`. Count the index pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` for which `nums1[i] + nums1[j]` is strictly greater than `nums2[i] + nums2[j]`, and return that count.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every pair is O(n²), too slow for `n = 10^5`. Move everything to one side: `nums1[i] + nums1[j] > nums2[i] + nums2[j]` is the same as `diff[i] + diff[j] > 0` with `diff[k] = nums1[k] - nums2[k]`. Now each index is a single number, and the order of the pair no longer matters, so we may sort `diff` and count pairs with a positive sum using two pointers from both ends.

## Approach

1. Build `diff[i] = nums1[i] - nums2[i]` and sort it ascending.
2. Put `left` at the start and `right` at the end.
3. If `diff[left] + diff[right] > 0`, then `diff[right]` also works with every index from `left` to `right - 1` (they are all at least `diff[left]`), so add `right - left` pairs and move `right` down.
4. Otherwise `diff[left]` is too small even for the largest partner, so it fits no pair; move `left` up.
5. Stop when the pointers meet and return `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

`diff = [1, -1, 1, -1]`, sorted `[-1, -1, 1, 1]`. `left = 0, right = 3`: `-1 + 1 = 0`, not positive, so `left = 1`. Again `0`, so `left = 2`. Now `1 + 1 = 2 > 0`: add `3 - 2 = 1` and `right = 2`. The pointers meet; the answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n): sorting dominates; the two-pointer scan is O(n).
- Space: O(n) for `diff`.

## Pitfalls

- The comparison is strict: a pair whose sums are equal is not counted.
- Sorting the original arrays separately breaks the pairing; sort only the combined `diff` values.
- The count can reach about n²/2 (around 5·10^9), which overflows a 32-bit integer; use a 64-bit type in Java or C.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of the arrays |
| `diff` | sorted values of `nums1[i] - nums2[i]` |
| `left`, `right` | pointers to the smallest and largest unpaired candidates |
| `count` | number of good pairs found so far |
